To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the modified Gompertz equation is an appropriate model to classify the anaerobic bioremediation of HCPs based on ABI.
the anaerobic bioreactors can be used for the classification of HCPs based on anaerobe biodegradability.
the anaerobic degradable household chemicals can be classified based on their biodegradability and that the classification is a function of their composition and concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an ABI classification of HCPs, which is based on their biodegradability in anaerobic conditions and can be used for the assessment of the performance of anaerobic reactors treating domestic sewage.

the development of a new method for assessing the biodegradablity of HCPs, which is a crucial step towards their environmental risk assessment and the development of more efficient and environmentally friendly wastewater treatment systems.
developing a classification system for HCPs based on anaerobically degradable properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anaerobic bioreactors are capable of degrading HCPs with ABI VI, V, and IV.
the anaerobic bioreactors would not be able to treat HCPs with ABI 0, ABI 1 and ABI 2.
the anaerobic bioreactors would not be capable of degrading HCPs in ABI 0 and 1 classes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study provides an innovative approach to classify household chemical products (HCPS) based on their anaerobic biogradability.
the anaerobic bioreactors have a higher tolerance towards ABI VI, whereas ABI V and ABI IV can be tolerated by anaerobic and aerobic systems respectively.
the ABI can be used as an effective and simple tool for the classification of HCPs in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ABI can be used as a tool to identify HCPs with high anaerobic biorecalcitrance and can help to identify the most recalcitrant compounds and their sources in the wastewater treatment system and in the environment in general.
a classification system based on anaerobi biodegradability can help to identify HCPs with low degradability and hence can be regulated.

the ABI approach can be used as a screening tool for HCPs to assess their anaerobic biogeochemical fate in the environment and can be used to design and implement appropriate wastewater treatment systems.
